title: Representability and smoothness of torsors under smooth affine groups
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $S$ be a $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $G\to S$ be an affine, smooth, finitely presented group scheme [pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]: its multiplication, inverse and identity are $S$-morphisms satisfying the group axioms. Write $h_G$ for its sheaf of points on $S$-schemes for the fppf topology. Let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on this site with a left $h_G$-action. Assume there is an fppf covering family $\{S_a\to S\}$ [def-pc-fppf-site] and equivariant isomorphisms $F|_{S_a}\simeq h_{G\times_SS_a}$ for left translation. Then $F\simeq h_P$ for a scheme $P$ over $S$, and $P\to S$ is affine, smooth, surjective, and universally open (every base change is open on underlying spaces). The action is represented and $G\times_SP\to P\times_SP$, $(g,p)\mapsto(gp,p)$, is an isomorphism. The assertions include the trivial group scheme and arbitrary, possibly nonreduced, $S$. All schemes, sheaves and covering index sets are in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]; fibre products are as in [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 049C (remark-fun-with-torsors), affirmative answer to (2) for affine groups, via affine descent; descent.tex Tag 02VL (lemma-descending-property-smooth); morphisms.tex Tag 056G (lemma-smooth-open). This statement includes the geometric properties of the descended torsor, not just the torsor definition of Tag 049B.

proof.text: Choose the given equivariant trivializations $t_a:F|_{S_a}\simeq h_{G_a}$, where $G_a=G\times_SS_a$. On $S_{ab}=S_a\times_SS_b$, the natural bijection $t_b t_a^{-1}$ between the two represented restrictions gives by [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] a unique scheme isomorphism $\phi_{ab}:G_a\times_SS_b\simeq S_a\times_SG_b$. On triple overlaps $(t_c t_b^{-1})(t_b t_a^{-1})=t_c t_a^{-1}$; faithfulness gives the scheme cocycle. Thus the $G_a$ and $\phi_{ab}$ form the family descent datum of [def-trf-scheme-cover-descent-datum]. The identity condition follows from $t_a t_a^{-1}=1$. No choice of group-valued transition element is needed.

source.place: Tag 049C, remark-fun-with-torsors, answer (2); descent datum made explicit as in descent.tex Tags 023U and 023X

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fppf-family-coproduct-descent-encoding] to this family. It supplies $A=\coprod_aS_a$, $Z=\coprod_aG_a$, an fpqc singleton $q:A\to S$, and a descent datum $D$ on $Z/A$. The canonical map $Z\to G\times_SA$ is an isomorphism: over the disjoint open component $S_a$ it is the identity of $G_a$; the component inverses glue uniquely, and their composites are identities because they are so on the component cover. The components form a disjoint open cover by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]; their inverse images cover the fibre product. Morphism gluing and equality on this open cover are [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Hence $Z\to A$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], being the base change of $G\to S$. This uses the encoding lemma for arbitrary set-indexed families, not an assumption that $q$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0245, lemma-affine; Tag 023X, lemma-family-is-one; topologies.tex Tag 022C

proof.text: By [lem-galois-fpqc-affine-descent-effective] the affine datum $D$ is effective. The same-scheme clause of [lem-trf-fppf-family-coproduct-descent-encoding] yields a scheme $P/S$ and compatible isomorphisms $P\times_SS_a\simeq G_a$ realizing the original $\phi_{ab}$. For every $T/S$ and $s\in F(T)$, its restrictions to $T_a=T\times_SS_a$ give morphisms $T_a\to P$ via $t_a$ and these isomorphisms. Compatibility is exactly the defining equality for $\phi_{ab}$. They glue to a unique $T\to P$ by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc] and [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent]. Conversely, a map $T\to P$ gives compatible sections of $F(T_a)$, which glue by the assumed sheaf axiom. The two operations are inverse on every $T_a$, hence inverse globally by uniqueness. Uniqueness also proves naturality in $T$. Thus $F\simeq h_P$. The fact that $h_P$ is an fppf sheaf follows from those same two cited statements; there is no additional representability assumption.

source.place: Tag 049C via descent.tex Tag 0245 (lemma-affine), Tag 023Q (lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms); topologies.tex Tag 022C

proof.text: Transfer the left $h_G$-action to $h_P$. Since $h_{G\times_SP}=h_G\times h_P$ by the fibre-product universal property, [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] represents it by a morphism $a:G\times_SP\to P$. The action equations hold as scheme equations by faithfulness. On $S_a$ the map $\alpha=(a,\mathrm{pr}_P)$ is $(g,y)\mapsto(gy,y)$ on $G_a\times G_a$ and has inverse $(x,y)\mapsto(xy^{-1},y)$. For a pair of sections of $P$ on $T$, these local inverses produce the unique local $g$ satisfying $gp_2=p_1$. On overlaps the $g$'s agree by that uniqueness. As $h_G$ is an fppf sheaf by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc] and [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], they glue to a unique global $g$. This constructs a natural inverse on all test schemes; Yoneda makes it a scheme inverse to $\alpha$.

The cover $\{S_a\to S\}$ is fpqc by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. Each $P\times_SS_a\to S_a$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], since it is isomorphic to the base change $G_a\to S_a$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-affine] gives that $P\to S$ is affine. Smoothness of $G_a\to S_a$ is base-change stability in [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality], specialized to schemes (identity etale charts). Its fppf target-locality clause then gives smoothness of $P\to S$. For surjectivity, the identity section of $G_a$ gives a section of $P\times_SS_a\to S_a$; composition with $P\times_SS_a\to P$ shows that the image of $P\to S$ contains the image of every $S_a\to S$. These images cover $S$, so $P\to S$ is surjective. This argument does not assert that $P(T)$ is nonempty for every $T$.

By [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion], the smooth morphism $P\to S$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]: it is open after every base change, which is the asserted universal openness. Nothing in the preceding arguments assumed $S$ reduced or Noetherian. For the trivial group, each local $P\times_SS_a$ is $S_a$ and the unique transition is the identity; the section-gluing bijection in Step 3 identifies $F$ with $h_S$. For $S=\varnothing$, the empty covering and the same sheaf axiom give $P=\varnothing$.

Statement change: 'translation on the right' became left action and left translation. This matches Stacks groupoids Tag 0498 (left action, (g,x)↦(a(g,x),x), trivial = left multiplication). The base text was inconsistent: for constant S_3, x↦xg is not a left action. The right-torsor reading would be equivalent via p·g^{-1}, so nothing is weakened, and the only citer (nodal-normalization-picard-sequence step 6, commutative torus) is unaffected. Step 1: Yoneda on Sch/S_ab gives φ_ab and the cocycle, matching def-trf-scheme-cover-descent-datum. Step 2: the encoding lemma (fppf family, infinite I, no qc) gives A, Z and D; Z≅G×_SA follows from the coproduct and gluing leaves, so Z→A is affine by base change. Step 3: affine fpqc descent (singleton fpqc, affine) plus the same-scheme clause give P with ψ_b=φ_abψ_a; I checked the gluing of sections via fppf⇒fpqc and representable descent, and the inverse via the sheaf axiom of F. Step 4: the local inverse (xy^{-1},y) holds in the noncommutative case, and g glues in h_G. Step 5: 02L5 for affineness; the same-unit space smooth locality node (no qc) for smoothness, since the scheme-level lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent needs a qc cover; surjectivity via the identity section. Step 6: smooth⇒flat+lfp⇒universally open. Edge cases checked: S empty, trivial group, nonreduced S, a torsor with no S-points. No duplicate found in the DAG. Advisory: lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-representability-descent-data could have shortened Step 3. Declared tool_uses (trf descent datum, encoding, galois affine descent, pbc 02L5, sbc criterion) are generic and accepted. Batch-5: the three trf citations are a general definition, a Mathlib-leaf topology fact and descent bookkeeping, none part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so accepted. No SGA.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_affine_group_torsor_representability (k : Type u) [Field k] (S : Scheme.{u}) (_s : S ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (G : Over S) [GrpObj G] [IsAffineHom G.hom] [Smooth G.hom] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.hom] (F : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type (u + 1))) (act : ∀ T : Over S, (T ⟶ G) → F.obj.obj (op T) → F.obj.obj (op T)) (one_act : ∀ (T : Over S) (x : F.obj.obj (op T)), act T 1 x = x) (mul_act : ∀ (T : Over S) (g h : T ⟶ G) (x : F.obj.obj (op T)), act T (g * h) x = act T g (act T h x)) (map_act : ∀ (T T' : Over S) (f : T' ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ G) (x : F.obj.obj (op T)), F.obj.map f.op (act T g x) = act T' (f ≫ g) (F.obj.map f.op x)) (locally_trivial : ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (U : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ S), Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ Scheme.fppfPrecoverage S ∧ ∀ i, ∃ e : (Over.map (f i)).op ⋙ F.obj ≅ (Over.map (f i)).op ⋙ uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.obj G, ∀ (T : Over (U i)) (g : (Over.map (f i)).obj T ⟶ G) (x : F.obj.obj (op ((Over.map (f i)).obj T))), (e.hom.app (op T) (act ((Over.map (f i)).obj T) g x)).down = lift g (e.hom.app (op T) x).down ≫ μ[G]) : ∃ (P : Over S) (e : F.obj ≅ uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.obj P) (a : ModObj G P), IsAffineHom P.hom ∧ Smooth P.hom ∧ Surjective P.hom ∧ UniversallyOpen P.hom ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (g : T ⟶ G) (x : F.obj.obj (op T)), (e.hom.app (op T) (act T g x)).down = lift g (e.hom.app (op T) x).down ≫ a.smul) ∧ IsIso (lift a.smul (snd G P))
